# ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io Weekly Report (Jan 4 - 10, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week's activity was characterized by deep technical investigation into protocol stability and ecosystem expansion through new token listings. While no major features were merged, significant progress was made in diagnosing critical issues, including L2 reorg handling in Kona and a bug in `eth_simulatev1` affecting OP Stack chains. Discussions centered on strengthening the protocol's resilience and correctness. In parallel, work continued to grow the Superchain ecosystem with pull requests to add new tokens to Base and Celo.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
Development efforts focused on expanding the token lists for chains within the Superchain ecosystem.

- **Superchain Token List Expansion:**
  - Pull requests were opened to add the DUAL token to the Base network ([#1252](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1252)), weETH and wstETH addresses for the Celo network ([#1251](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1251)), and the DeepNode token ([#1253](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/pull/1253)). These additions enhance the utility and interoperability of assets across the Superchain.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The week saw no new issues opened, but intense discussion continued on several critical active issues, laying the groundwork for future fixes.

- **Closed Issues:**
  - **OP Stack Compatibility Clarified:** An issue regarding OP Stack compatibility with Base-style minimal contracts ([#18709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18709)) was closed, confirming that smart contracts are generally compatible and providing a reference to documentation on differences from L1 Ethereum.

- **New & Active Issues:**
  - **Protocol Stability Under Investigation:** A significant discussion unfolded around L2 reorgs caused by L1 reorgs in Kona ([#18676](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18676)). The root cause analysis identified issues with stale caching in the L1 Origin Selector and a lack of proper reset logic. Proposed solutions involve strengthening Kona's L1 handling to be more robust, similar to `op-node`.
  - **Critical `eth_simulatev1` Bug:** The investigation into `eth_simulatev1` returning an error since the Jovian fork ([#739](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/739)) remains a high priority. This bug impacts backrunning strategies on OP Stack chains, and a potential fix has been identified in an `op-geth` pull request.
  - **RPC Endpoint Correction:** Discussion continued on the `optimism_syncStatus` RPC endpoint ([#18673](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18673)), which incorrectly reports the latest L1 head instead of the derivation cursor. The focus is on correcting this behavior without introducing additional complexity.
  - **Dispute Game Interface Enhancement:** The issue to extend the `IDisputeGame` interface for interoperability ([#18516](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18516)) was reopened to address remaining implementation details, indicating continued progress on the fault-proof system.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was evident in the detailed, cross-repository problem-solving on active issues. The discussion on the `eth_simulatev1` bug ([#739](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/739)) highlighted collaboration with the `op-geth` team, where a potential fix is being developed. Similarly, the in-depth analysis of Kona's reorg handling ([#18676](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18676)) showcased a strong collaborative effort to diagnose and propose fixes for a complex protocol-level issue. Active follow-up from contributors on issues like [#18516](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/18516) demonstrates a healthy and engaged maintenance process.
